purpose: Independent data-only review of the additive blockdev descriptor-aware mock; generic runner results establish no coverage.
scope: Review each frozen build, mode and completed assertion independently. Preserve previous evidence and reached failures. Synthetic success, EIO/EPERM ioctl and EIO/EPERM close cases do not replace evidence for other failure paths.
required_prerequisites: Before guest execution require an independently reviewed controller-owned teardown boundary that survives observer failure or runner timeout, can terminate and reap the complete owned scope including a tracee before its first ptrace stop, and records identity, deadline, signals, wait status and writer quiescence. Include independently reviewed normal-exit, initial-stop-timeout and forced-cleanup controls. WNOHANG and EXITKILL alone do not prove an uninterruptible child was reaped. Missing, late or unverified containment must not authorize the run.

Bind exact suite, helper and guard hashes, protected controller identity, image and frozen candidate provenance, uid/gid 2000, the native x86-64 syscall ABI, isolated private HOME and CASE, complete relevant runner records and guest teardown. Check actual tracee access to journals and captures and the per-channel pipe binding below; protect records from any actual independent writer within the owned scope. The scratch directory and candidate must be single-task with no uncontrolled writer or path replacement during each entry decision. A missing protection or isolation witness is infrastructure inconclusive for affected claims.

For each reached mode independently validate its bounded JSONL lines, total size, contiguous unique sequence, previous-line SHA-256 chain, monotonic times, header and per-mode binding, plus every relevant raw syscall-entry, exit, resume, next-stop, descriptor and incremental pipe-drain checkpoint. Verify stream offsets, base64 bytes, lengths, digests and pipe/capture inode identities. An intact run-end, both observed pipe EOFs, complete stable capture and naturally reaped child establish a completed mode; a completed behavioral assertion may be established at an earlier fully protected call boundary as specified below. A malformed or partial suffix, limit, interrupted stop, index error or pending reap is infrastructure inconclusive for the affected stage, not automatically for an already qualified prefix.

Verify each native and candidate executable and argv, root-owned non-writable executable and parent path, pinned digest/dev/inode/size, initial PID and raw starttime, successful same-PID exec entry and exit, actual proc executable identity and post-exec protected digest. Bind candidate digest to controller frozen-build provenance and native executable to image provenance. Missing or ambiguous executable or task identity is infrastructure inconclusive.

Verify each initial mock object was atomically created with O_EXCL and O_NOFOLLOW as a private regular inode and pinned read-only. Every registered open must be rewritten at entry to fcntl(F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC) of the matching inherited pin, original arguments restored and nonnegative returned descriptor verified against the pin. The kernel must never execute the operand-path open. Inspect each actual pre-marker startup open for a root-protected non-writable allowed regular runtime target and retained resolved identity. Require the necessary shared native path controls below, no real device opens or ioctls, and no relevant unsupported alternate open, process creation, descriptor escape, path mutation, network or namespace operation.

For every emulated open, injected ioctl, close or denied guarded truncate independently validate same-PID syscall entry and exit, arguments, successful skip/rewrite, actual kernel return, post-mutation register readback, successful PTRACE_SYSCALL resume without delivered signal, and following same-PID syscall-entry stop or natural exit. For a skipped x86-64 syscall require the recorded orig_rax=-1 and actual skipped result consistent with -ENOSYS before the injected negative return, and independently verify the signed injected RAX. For pinned-fcntl open require restored RAX equal the actual signed fcntl return and bind the returned fd to its pin. An intended value alone is not proof of delivery.

Reconstruct bounded stdout and stderr independently from observer-drained pipe journal chunks and the separate observer-owned per-mode captures when both are complete, with correct offsets, sizes, hashes, bindings and writer protection. For each claim check the relevant channel binding and a stream-barrier for each relied-on channel after the completed relevant write: the same tracee is stopped, that pipe has been drained to EAGAIN or EOF, and the required bytes through that boundary were journaled before resume. A drain performed while the tracee runs alone does not prove an assertion boundary. Separate streams alone do not establish their relative order; use stopped-task checkpoints and syscall order. Retain incomplete raw prefixes but do not infer missing bytes or completion. Decode the builtin status from FD_MOCK_RESULT; the outer shell intentionally exits 0 and the generic observed marker is not the blockdev status.

Before qualifying candidate conclusions, validate the same-invocation native TRUNCATE and PATHS shared safety controls and their raw stop records, not only observer labels. Validate each native stream sensitivity control only for the output channel on which the particular assertion depends, while checking for any actual shared fault. Other native subcontrols are per assertion as below; do not borrow across frozen builds, suite invocations, guests or observer instances. An absent or failed shared safety control makes dependent assertions inconclusive; an unrelated subcontrol failure does not by itself invalidate a different, fully qualified assertion.

shared_native_safety.truncate_and_capture: Require the exclusively created private sentinel inode and its fixed bytes, identity and metadata in truncate-sentinel-before and truncate-sentinel-after; both must be stable and equal. In the same native trace require one expected ftruncate(1,0) on the bound stdout pipe and one expected truncate of the private sentinel to be skipped and return EPERM, with entry/rewrite/exit/readback/resume/next-stop evidence. Require the complete FD_MOCK_CAPTURE_SENTINEL line to remain at the start of native stdout and the independently captured FD_MOCK_NATIVE_TRUNCATE JSON to report both errno values as EPERM. Check that ftruncate targets the bound stdout pipe, which is distinct from the observer-only regular capture inode. The summary alone cannot prove protection. If the sensitivity control, sentinel bytes, relevant prefix or writer isolation fails, do not authorize dependent candidate conclusions.
shared_native_safety.path_ownership: Require the same native invocation's FD_MOCK_NATIVE_PATHS checkpoint and raw syscall records to show ENOENT for an unregistered path and EPERM for the D symlink and E replacement; inspect creation, lstat and pin identities and prove no substituted pathname was opened. Reconstruct the registered pin and fd generations needed by each conclusion. An unproved shared object safety boundary is inconclusive.
shared_native_safety.guard_scope_and_unexpected_operations: Pathname truncate on an evidence file or an unresolved/aliased path is suppressed before kernel execution; only a proven distinct direct private regular CASE inode can be passed through. ftruncate is suppressed when its kernel-normalized fd resolves to a held or named evidence inode or either inherited output pipe, including aliases; unrelated fds remain outside that denial. Independently inspect the recorded mutation_guard, raw entry and exit and expected_control fields. Any unexpected candidate truncate or ftruncate, whether denied or allowed, is instrumentation/inconclusive for behavior dependent on that operation or a possibly affected prefix; it is not a product FAIL. Preserve a previously completed protected mismatch if its own evidence and safety are unaffected. Reject the x32 syscall-number bit before x86-64 dispatch; an attempted unsupported ABI is instrumentation inconclusive for dependent stages.
shared_native_safety.observer_drained_streams: For each relevant mode validate stream-setup: separate FIFO identities, a nonblocking read end held by the observer, a blocking write end given to the child, and an exclusively created private O_APPEND regular capture held by the observer. Check parent-pipe-writers-closed and the initial stopped-child stream-binding, its full descriptor inventory and raw fdinfo: fd 1 and fd 2 must be their respective write-only pipe inodes and the child must hold no regular capture or journal descriptor. Trace the actual subsequent open, descriptor and stream-rebinding events through the particular assertion, including aliases, and disqualify only the affected channel/prefix if it could have bypassed or replaced the bound pipe or reached observer-owned evidence. Validate each stream chunk and stopped-writer stream-barrier against its pipe and capture identities, offsets and raw stop; each relied-on pipe must be drained to EAGAIN or EOF at its own barrier; preserve a completed unaffected channel barrier even if draining the other channel fails later. The pipe is not seekable or mappable as an ordinary regular file, so positional write, seek plus write, hole punching and writable shared mappings cannot rewrite prior pipe bytes. No extra rule forbids unrelated descriptor operations. Before a channel-dependent conclusion, use that channel's same-invocation native pwrite and lseek sensitivity checks: require the actual unsuppressed x86-64 pwrite64 and lseek entry/exit to return -ESPIPE and the matching FD_MOCK_NATIVE_STREAM errno values. Check the intact stdout capture sentinel or stderr begin prefix for the respective channel. A false or unavailable control is infrastructure inconclusive for that channel, not product FAIL; do not invalidate another channel solely because of it if actual shared faults are excluded. The raw observations and relevant pipe binding, not the summary boolean alone, are the evidence.

native_control_dependencies.ioctl_eio: For an EIO ioctl conclusion, use the native A first GETSS control: raw skipped ioctl and delivered -EIO, plus the corresponding EIO result in FD_MOCK_NATIVE_IOCTL. Require the success portion of this checkpoint only where the particular conclusion uses synthetic successful values or continued successful GETSS.
native_control_dependencies.ioctl_eperm: For an EPERM ioctl conclusion, use the native A second GETSS control: raw skipped ioctl and delivered -EPERM, plus the corresponding EPERM result in FD_MOCK_NATIVE_IOCTL. Require the success control only for a conclusion that uses it.
native_control_dependencies.ioctl_success: For a successful synthetic GETSS/value conclusion, require the native third GETSS return 0 and 512 value, the relevant raw stop/readback and attributable FD_MOCK_NATIVE_IOCTL bytes. GETSIZE is an eight-byte source emulation, whereas this native success control exercises four-byte GETSS; bind any GETSIZE output assertion to its actual traced emulation and byte provenance.
native_control_dependencies.close_eio: For A close-EIO conclusions require FD_MOCK_NATIVE_CLOSE_EIO and raw native evidence for successful actual A close, injected -EIO, resumed delivery, EBADF on that descriptor, reuse for C, unrelated C ioctl ENOTTY and normal C close. Independently track fd generations and correlate the reported values.
native_control_dependencies.close_eperm: For A close-EPERM conclusions require FD_MOCK_NATIVE_CLOSE_EPERM and raw native evidence for successful actual B close, injected -EPERM, resumed delivery, EBADF, reuse for the new B fd and its normal close. Independently track fd generations and correlate the reported values.
native_control_dependencies.identity: For open-file-description identity only, require the observer-side native dup same-description kcmp control to compare equal, separate open of the same pinned inode to compare unequal, successful pidfd_getfd for every relevant before/after descriptor and per-number kcmp results. Denied or unavailable identity capability is inconclusive only for the identity claim, not automatically for an r4 status or diagnostic or a bounded descriptor-number/count observation.

per_assertion_dependencies.close_eio_diagnostic_or_status: After shared safety and exact candidate identity, require the relevant native close_eio controls, proof the candidate closed its actual A fd successfully before injected EIO, signed register readback, resume/next-stop, and complete protected bytes through the returned builtin marker. Assess device/close/errno diagnostic and FD_MOCK_RESULT=1 separately. This assertion does not require the native B close-EPERM/reuse control or kcmp.
per_assertion_dependencies.close_eperm_diagnostic_or_status: Use shared safety plus native close_eperm controls and the candidate A real-close-then-EPERM delivery, complete diagnostic bytes and returned status marker. A separate A EIO control failure does not by itself defeat this assertion if the trace excludes a shared fault.
per_assertion_dependencies.close_error_later_device: For either qualified close-error mode, use the corresponding close control, candidate A close/delivery and complete call-level trace/bytes to establish whether B was processed after A. A fully returned call omitting required B work is a product mismatch, not a missing native control. Close occurs after the A actions; do not demand an invented A action after its close.
per_assertion_dependencies.ioctl_error: Use shared safety, the corresponding native ioctl_eio or ioctl_eperm control and candidate A GETSIZE failure delivery. Determine each diagnostic, FD_MOCK_RESULT=1, later A GETSS action and later B actions separately from complete attributable streams and syscall order; require the success control for any claim that depends on successful synthetic results.
per_assertion_dependencies.all_success: Use shared safety and relevant native successful ioctl control, actual candidate emulation/delivery for the exercised requests, attributable complete output and FD_MOCK_RESULT=0. This is limited to the exercised synthetic modes.
per_assertion_dependencies.descriptor_count: For the specific completed mode require shared safety and the corresponding native control: close_eio for close-EIO, close_eperm for close-EPERM, the matching ioctl control for an injected ioctl error, or ioctl_success for the synthetic success mode. Prove the actual candidate event and then use same-PID/start complete before and after inventories and the relevant fd-generation trace to establish a no-net-count-increase observation or equality of number sets. Equal counts or numbers do not prove unchanged open-file descriptions or all failure paths; apply pidfd_getfd/kcmp controls only for that stronger claim.

completed_assertions_and_preservation: An assertion boundary must independently establish the controls and exact injected event it depends on, the returned builtin or other required completed action, and all relevant bytes through that boundary in a protected verified journal prefix. Bind the relevant channel and a stopped-tracee stream-barrier through the required bytes; a missing diagnostic requires a complete stderr prefix through the point by which it was required. Absence from a partial or unverified stream is not proof. An incomplete later marker, later native subcontrol, later mode, final index or cleanup cannot retroactively erase an already established independent mismatch.

If native A close-EIO, EBADF, C reuse, ENOTTY and shared safety are established, a false or missing later native B-only close-EPERM reuse result does not itself suppress a candidate A close-EIO diagnostic or status FAIL. Check for actual shared observer, task identity, protected-record or lifecycle faults before treating that B result as unrelated. B-EPERM-dependent claims remain inconclusive.

Natural reaping, both observed pipe EOFs and complete captures are required to call an entire mode complete. A later forced cleanup or incomplete mode is separately an infrastructure incident; it does not automatically revoke a prior call-level mismatch whose own stage, controls, stream barrier and independently protected bytes were already complete. Pending reap or absent teardown is never presumed safe, and no later or missing stage may be inferred.

A completed mismatch with all necessary controls is a product FAIL. Preserve it even when other assertions are inconclusive. Missing controls, unsupported operations, protection gaps, malformed relevant prefix, unproved return delivery, capture limits or ambiguous identity are infrastructure inconclusive for dependent claims, never a synthetic product FAIL.
preservation: Original r4: Injected ioctl errors EIO and EPERM and an injected close() error are reported per device/action and set aggregate failure without aborting later actions. Existing migration-blockdev-injected-errors EIO/EPERM evidence remains; its close error was not attempted.

Original r5: Descriptor cleanup: after success and after each failure path, the shell has no additional open descriptors. Existing fd-count evidence for real failures, injected errors and successful queries remains; close-error cleanup was not tested. This proposal does not independently establish every failure path.

Each mode has its own exclusively-created append-only bounded journal and observer-only regular captures. Two nonblocking observer pipe readers drain tracee output both during waits and at stops; stream chunks and stopped-writer drain barriers retain append order per channel. Earlier completed files are never overwritten. If a later run, output read, stop, reap, index save or journal limit fails, preserve independently validated earlier records and protected complete prefixes. A reached mismatch is creditable only if its own native controls, attribution, integrity, relevant channel binding/barrier and stage-completion prerequisites are complete; missing later results are inconclusive. Source prediction alone is not behavioral coverage.
limitations: No VM, fixture, native control, candidate or reference code was run. Ptrace rewriting, both truncate guards, pipe binding and drain/EOF behavior, per-channel pwrite/lseek sensitivity, sentinel controls, actual close semantics, guest runtime files, scheduling and journal/output limits remain unverified.

WNOHANG polling does not bound filesystem writes, fsync, process startup or scheduling. A separately reviewed controller containment, teardown and protected-record witness remains mandatory before guest execution.

The primary must independently implement and review this data-only per-assertion gate. Source fixes, partial raw observations, generic runner output and covers=[] provide no new coverage or product PASS.
